sentences: `image_gather4_l(_o)`: no explicit-LOD gather in core Vulkan, so four `OpImageFetch` at the mip the "Gather sampler LOD" row chooses, in gather order.
`image_gather4_l(_o)`: no explicit-LOD gather in core Vulkan, so four `OpImageFetch` at mip `Floor(clamp(LOD, S# MIN_LOD, MAX_LOD) + 0.5)` (ties up, as native) in gather order.
With `d16` those four taps round to binary16 and pack low half first into two consecutive VGPRs.
The packed words and the first untouched VGPR were checked with `ps_gather_wrap.asm` on RTX 5080 and Radeon Graphics.

Each of the four texel coordinates goes through the S#'s own address mode, read from S# word0 (`CLAMP_X` = bits [2:0], `CLAMP_Y` = [5:3]; fields from Mesa `src/amd/registers/gfx10-rsrc.json`, values `SQ_TEX_*` in Mesa `gfx6.json`, matching RADV's `radv_tex_wrap` mapping of Vulkan address modes): 0 wrap (`c mod n`), 1 mirror (`c mod 2n`, reflected), 2 clamp to the last texel, 3 mirror-once (`-1-c` for negative `c`, then clamped), as in Vulkan's address-mode definitions.
The modulo is `OpSRem` plus the period when the remainder is negative, not `OpSMod`.

On a Ryzen 5 7600's iGPU (RDNA2) with AMD's Windows driver 24.10.24, `OpSMod` of a negative coordinate came out with the dividend's sign: the three `ps_gather_wrap` cases whose wrap or mirror coordinate is negative (1, 2 and 6) fetched outside the image and read zeros, while the same module passed on an RTX 4070 SUPER.
With `OpSRem` and the fix-up, all 4096 pixels are exact on both.
A literal S# (`s_mov_b32` earlier in the block) is decoded at translation time; otherwise the mode is read from the SGPR at run time.

A literal S# with a border mode (4-7: half-border, border colour) or `FORCE_UNNORMALIZED` is `Unsupported`; a run-time S# can't be judged, so modes 4-7 act as clamp-to-edge there and `FORCE_UNNORMALIZED` (word0 bit 15) is not applied (coordinates are still scaled by the image size).

Modes 6 (clamp border) and 7 (mirror once border) give a tap whose coordinate, before the clamp, is outside [0, n-1] on either axis the S# border colour's channel instead of the fetched texel: BORDER_COLOR_TYPE = word 3 [31:30] (Mesa `gfx10-rsrc.json` `SQ_IMG_SAMP_WORD3`, `SQ_TEX_BORDER_COLOR_*` in `gfx6.json`), 0 transparent black, 1 opaque black (alpha 1), 2 opaque white; 1 for an integer format, as Vulkan's `INT_OPAQUE_*`.

Type 3 (a colour from the border-colour table, `BORDER_COLOR_PTR`) is `Unsupported` on a literal S# and transparent black at run time (SHADER-348: since #1567 made the game's S# words literals, 16 of the corpus's mode-6 gathers failed as `Unsupported`; before that they ran as clamp-to-edge).

A literal S# with a half-border mode (4, 5) or `FORCE_UNNORMALIZED` is `Unsupported`; a run-time S# can't be judged, so modes 4 and 5 act as clamp-to-edge there and `FORCE_UNNORMALIZED` (word0 bit 15) is not applied (coordinates are still scaled by the image size).

Those two, and a table border colour (BORDER_COLOR_TYPE 3) on a run-time S#, which gives transparent black, are the remaining approximations; the unnormalized rules (texel-unit coordinates, mip 0) weren't confirmed on hardware, so they were not guessed.

GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/ps_gather_wrap.asm` (`vk_texture_test`; expected values derived by hand in its header; six border cases, three literal and three run-time S#) on AMD (Radeon 880M, wave64) and NVIDIA RTX 5070.
